text:
Taylor (People Ops): Quick thread  Priyanka accepted but is still abroad doing consular stamping. She asked if she can start remotely from India while waiting for visa slot (could be 612+ weeks). Thoughts on payroll, benefits, security clearance? cc @Priya (immig)
Noah (Hiring Manager): Team wants her to start on 2026-10-01 if possible. OK with remote initial period, but need to confirm legal/payroll/security.
Priyanka (Candidate): Hi all  I can start remote part-time from India. My consular appointment earliest is mid-Nov. I wanted to know if Redwood can employ me remotely abroad and how benefits/taxation would work.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): From an immigration angle: if Priyanka is outside the US and not in US immigration status, she cannot perform US-based employment that requires US work authorization. However, some companies hire remote overseas employees as international employees (local contract) or as contractors. That has payroll, tax, and IP considerations. We cannot have her work as a US employee until she has US work authorization (visa stamped and admitted).
Ben (Payroll): Important: payroll has two paths: 1) hire her as US employee (requires I-9, presence in US, and work authorization) OR 2) engage via our international payroll provider (local entity/PE) or contractor arrangement. Both require approvals. Contractor has compliance risk and benefits differences. Global Mobility must confirm local labor rules in India.
Sara (Global Mobility): We use RemoteCo (vendor) for India hires. We can onboard her as an employee of RemoteCo on our behalf (EOR) and second her back, or as a contractor depending on her preference and true work relationship. Cost + benefits differ. I can get a quote and timeline.
Alex (Security): Note for roles requiring access to source code or internal prod systems, we have different rules for remote foreign contractors vs employees. Some systems require additional approvals or restrict access until on US payroll with background check. We need to map required access and do a risk review.
Taylor (People Ops): Action items: 1) Priya to confirm we cannot treat remote overseas work as US employment. 2) Sara to get EOR/contractor options and cost. 3) Ben to outline payroll/tax differences and forms. 4) Alex to provide list of access restrictions. 5) Priyanka to confirm preference (contractor via EOR vs wait for stamping).
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Confirmed: cannot onboard as US employee until she appears for I-9 in US and has authorization. We should avoid misclassification. If company wants her to start earlier, EOR is safest. Document: candidate cannot sign US-employment I-9 until physically present in US with documents.
Priyanka (Candidate): Thanks. I prefer Redwood employment but open to EOR if it helps start earlier. Curious about benefits—will EOR provide similar health benefits?
Sara (Global Mobility): EOR packages usually include local statutory benefits, sometimes basic healthcare. They won't match US employer-sponsored plans. We can also explore temporary contractor plus a relocation bonus to bridge benefits. I'll price both.
Ben (Payroll): Payroll note: US payroll taxes won't apply if she's on RemoteCo payroll. For contractor pay, we'd need contractor agreement and potentially 1099 issues if she later becomes US worker. Also watch for permanent establishment risk. I'll write options and tax treatment.
Alex (Security): I'll run quick access matrix. For remote non-US employees we often limit production secrets and require VPN constraints and device management. Can make temporary prod access read-only until she is on US payroll and background-checked.
Noah (Hiring Manager): Team ok with limited access initially; ramp tasks can be docs, design, code review that don't require secrets. Good compromise.
Taylor (People Ops): Ok I'll propose two timelines to Priyanka: A) start 10/01 via EOR with limited access and local benefits; B) delay start until visa stamping and US entry, onboard as US employee on 11/15. Priyanka, which do you prefer?
Priyanka (Candidate): I'd like A if EOR gives decent pay and a relocation sign-on. If not, I'd rather wait and start after stamping. Also my landlord in India needs notice by 10/15 so early start helps.
Sara (Global Mobility): I'll aim to get EOR quote and benefits summary by EOD tomorrow. Need final decision by Friday to set contracts.
Ben (Payroll): I'll draft payroll flows: EOR (RemoteCo invoice + gross-to-net example), Contractor (monthly invoice + withholding responsibilities), US hire (I-9, W-4, SSN required). Also note timekeeping differences.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): One more: if we onboard via EOR and later transfer her to US employment, ensure immigration process is the same (consular stamp + admission) and update contracts. No double counting of employment gaps.
Alex (Security): We'll prepare an onboarding checklist for limited access remote workers outside US. Includes background check feasibility (some countries limited) and MFA enrollment. If background check unavailable, additional manager approval required.
Taylor (People Ops): hr-bot: please DM Priyanka secure link to upload passport + resume for EOR onboarding if she chooses.
hr-bot: Sent secure onboarding link via DM. Do not post PII here.
Priyanka (Candidate): Received link 1 I'll upload docs tonight. Thanks.
Sara (Global Mobility): Quote update: RemoteCo can onboard in 7 business days. Cost ~ 18% on top of salary for statutory + admin. Healthcare is basic local plan; expat top-up not included. I'll attach exact numbers in DM.
Ben (Payroll): Scenarios doc posted in Drive: "India remote start options". Includes sample pay slips, tax treatment, and transfer checklist.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Final note: if candidate later receives H-1B or L visa, we will re-onboard as US employee and run I-9. The EOR period is separate employment. Keep documentation to show no unauthorized US employment occurred.
Noah (Hiring Manager): Sounds like route A is acceptable to the team. Priyanka, want us to proceed with EOR?
Priyanka (Candidate): Yes please proceed with EOR option. I'd like the relocation stipend included and to have limited access ramp plan. Happy to sign EOR contract.
Taylor (People Ops): Great 1 Sara please initiate RemoteCo onboarding and include relocation stipend proposal. Ben & Alex 1 please follow up on payroll and access flows. Priyanka please expect contract via RemoteCo and we'll loop you in.
Sara (Global Mobility): Starting onboarding now. Will loop in Priyanka and share timelines.
Taylor (People Ops): Closing loop 1 saved notes to People Ops drive and created task ticket #HR-5421. Welcome Priyanka!
Priyanka (Candidate): Thank you all 1 excited to get started.
